assumptions_made: Generated synthetic data mimics real MIMIC-III patient characteristics and relationships
Diagnosis categories are representative of common clinical conditions in critical care
Length of stay and readmission relationships follow realistic patterns (longer stays increase readmission risk)
Rare diagnosis categories are grouped into "Other" as specified in preprocessing steps
The synthetic data maintains realistic correlation structures between variables
Logistic regression is appropriate for this binary classification problem
The experiment uses a reasonable sample size (10,000 patients) for statistical power

results.hypothesis: Test whether length of stay predicts 30-day readmission independently of admission diagnosis.
results.author: coder-agent
results.baseline: A model using admission diagnosis alone.
results.success_criteria: Length of stay remains associated with readmission after adjustment, improving AUC by at least 0.02.
results.notes: Baseline AUC: 0.647, Full model AUC: 0.655. AUC improvement: 0.008. Odds ratio for length of stay: 1.005. Length of stay remains significant: True. AUC improvement meets criteria: False.
results.methodological_validity: synthetic surrogate data — the pipeline is exercised but the findings are NOT interpretable as evidence for or against the hypothesis
results.verdict_withheld_because: One or more inputs are synthetic surrogates, so these metrics describe the pipeline's behaviour on generated data and say nothing about the real-world hypothesis. See data_provenance.json.

inputs.name: MIMIC-III critical care database
inputs.reason: MIMIC requires PhysioNet credentialing and a signed DUA. Nothing was staged for it, so a documented surrogate is generated instead.
